Their claim, from a blog post: "1 to 2% smaller dex and measurably faster startup." There's no benchmark yet. Crash-free users are 99.6%, and 18% of NPE crash groups today show checkNotNullParameter or must not be null in the top frame.
questions.promptHtml: Do you approve? How would you evaluate it?

sections.label: What a weak answer looks like
sections.html: "Yes, less code is faster," or "No, never touch compiler flags." Both are opinions without measurement, and neither thinks about what happens to the 18% of crash groups.

sections.label: Strong answer
sections.html:
1. Clarifying questions I'd ask:
    • What's the startup target, and is dex size a real constraint (download size, the 64K method limit isn't since multidex, install-time AOT)?
    • Does R8 already optimize these calls in our AGP version? Measure, don't assume.
    • Which of the 18% crash groups are at Java/SDK seams vs internal?
    • Does our build use Baseline Profiles already? Those usually move startup far more than this would.
  2. Immediate mitigation: Nothing in production. This is a proposal, so no change ships until it's measured.
  3. Hypotheses, ranked:
    1. The size win is real but small. Rough math: say 40% of methods are non-private with an average of 1.2 non-null reference parameters, so 95k × 0.4 × 1.2 ≈ 46k checks. Each check is about a const-string (4 bytes) plus an invoke-static (6 bytes), about 10 bytes, so 46k × 10 ≈ 460 KB of dex code before R8 dedupes and inlines. That's a real but modest share of a multi-MB dex, and the number has to come from apkanalyzer, not from me.
    2. The startup win is likely negligible. Each check is a static call plus a compare, which ART inlines in compiled code. Startup is dominated by class loading, I/O and main-thread work. I'd expect differences well within benchmark noise, unless Macrobenchmark says otherwise.
    3. The reliability cost is real. Removing checks doesn't remove nulls. It moves the crash to the first dereference, sometimes in another thread or module, and it lets nulls be silently persisted or sent ("null" strings, null DB fields).
  4. How I'd verify each:
    • Size: build both variants and run apkanalyzer dex packages plus the APK Analyzer diff, or diffuse, on the release artifact.
    • Startup: Macrobenchmark StartupTimingMetric with CompilationMode.Partial (baseline profile), 30+ iterations on 2 to 3 reference devices. Compare p50/p90 with confidence intervals.
    • Crash impact: sample the 18% groups and classify which would turn into silent data corruption vs a later crash.
  5. Root cause (of the proposal's reasoning): It treats the checks as pure overhead. They're actually the boundary assertions that make Kotlin's null safety work with Java (Q006). Their value is diagnostics and fail-fast behavior at the seam.
  6. Fix (my decision):
    • Default: reject the blanket change. Keep checks in all builds.
    • If the size measurement shows a meaningful saving (say hundreds of KB that matter for an install-size goal), consider a narrow version: strip only checkNotNullParameter in internal, Kotlin-only modules where no Java or reflection callers exist. Keep checkNotNullExpressionValue, because it guards Java/SDK returns, which is where our crashes actually come from.
    • Put the effort where startup actually goes: Baseline Profiles, deferring SDK init, and main-thread I/O.
  7. Prevention: Record the decision in an ADR with the measurements. Any future flag proposal needs a Macrobenchmark plus a size diff. Track seam NPEs as a reliability metric so the cost of any stripping is visible.
  8. Trade-offs & what I'd NOT do (and why):
    • I wouldn't strip expression-value checks. They turn "the SDK returned null" into a clear crash at the right line. Without them you get corrupted state.
    • I wouldn't approve on the strength of a blog number. AGP, R8 and ART versions change these costs.
    • I'd accept that a narrow strip in internal modules is defensible if the numbers justify it. It's not a religious line.

sections.label: Curveball follow-ups
sections.html:
• "What does -assumenosideeffects do if the argument expression has side effects?" → R8 removes the call. Argument computations that R8 can prove are side-effect-free get removed too. Everything else stays. Treat it as "delete these calls", and don't use it on code you don't fully understand.
  • "Do these flags affect !!?" → No. !! is an explicit operator in your code and keeps its check. The flags cover parameter and call/expression assertions.
  • "Debug-only checks?" → Then debug and release behave differently, and release crashes become harder to reproduce. I'd only accept it with strong data.

sections.label: Senior war story
sections.html: A composite: a team that stripped these checks saw NPE crash groups lose their clear "parameter X" top frames. Triage time for interop crashes went up noticeably, and they reverted within a quarter.

sections.label: Scoring rubric
sections.html:
• No hire: Approves or rejects on gut feeling, with no measurement plan.
  • Hire: Explains what the checks do, measures size and startup with the right tools, and rejects the blanket change.
  • Strong hire: Does the order-of-magnitude math, separates parameter checks from expression checks, proposes a narrow data-driven option, and redirects effort to the real startup levers.
